input: This executive summary presents an overview of delivery performance at a contract packaging firm operating 2 plants with revenue of $77 million per year, drawing on a comprehensive evidence base of order records for 12 months encompassing 17816 orders. Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery performance stood at 86%, which falls short of the target of 95% by a gap of 9 percentage points, highlighting a significant performance challenge. A closer examination of the data reveals that Plant 2 accounts for 68% of late orders, underscoring its central role in the overall problem. Meanwhile, the order backlog currently stands at 2.9 weeks, compared with 1.9 weeks a year ago, indicating that the shortfall is growing rather than diminishing. Overtime cost amounted to $1.6 million last year, up 27% on the year before, reflecting the substantial expense the firm incurs in attempting to keep pace with demand. In terms of potential solutions, a scheduling system for all plants has been quoted at $283k, while Plant 2 alone has been quoted at $122k. An internal estimate, rather than a vendor figure, suggests that the overtime reduction at Plant 2 could be in the region of 15–20% in the first year. Against this background, the recommendation under consideration is to install the system at Plant 2 first and to hold the remaining plants until Plant 2 results are reported, a staged approach that would commit $122k to test the estimate where the problem is most concentrated, rather than $283k committed across the firm at once. The operations director owns the scheduling programme, and any wider installation would be a second decision, taken on the Plant 2 evidence when it is reported, as the estimate covers Plant 2 only and no saving is claimed for the other plants.
